name: How much extra storage do I need after opening my kitchen?

mainEntity.name: How much storage should I add when converting to an open-concept kitchen?
mainEntity.text: How much storage should I add when converting to an open-concept kitchen?

acceptedAnswer.text: Open-concept kitchens often need more storage than closed kitchens because there are fewer walls for upper cabinets and more visible surfaces to keep clean. The best plans add pantry space, drawer storage, tall utility cabinets, and concealed zones for small appliances, cleaning supplies, and daily clutter. If the kitchen includes an island, that is a strong place to add storage, but only if the island still leaves enough circulation room. The storage strategy should be part of the layout, not something added after the fact. Many homeowners regret removing walls without replacing the storage the wall used to provide. A successful open-concept design keeps the kitchen organized while preserving the clean, airy look that motivated the conversion in the first place.
acceptedAnswer.description: Usually more than you think. Open-concept kitchens show clutter, so the design should add pantry space, deeper drawers, tall cabinets, and island storage if possible. Without more storage, the room may feel less functional even if it looks bigger.
